data.title: Full Stack Developer | React.js, Node.js, Next.js | SaaS Platform Development
data.description: Remote worldwide SaaS development with React, Node.js and Next.js, including integration with KlickTipp. Advertised at $34.25/hour, over 30 hours/week and 6+ months; public page shows 50+ proposals and one hire.
data.notes: Návrh připraven, nebyl odeslán. Inzerát a rozpočet znovu ověřit před podáním nabídky.
data.match_notes: Přímá shoda React/Next.js/Node.js a API integrací: WebIntegrator, EmbedIT a Ersilia. KlickTipp není doložená dosavadní zkušenost; ověřit API a požadovaný rozsah. Potvrdit dostupnost přes 30 hodin týdně, sazbu po poplatcích a zda klient po jednom přijetí dál hledá.
data.proposal_text:
Hi,

Your React, Node.js and Next.js stack is close to the work I have been doing across product interfaces and backend integrations, and I would be interested in helping with the SaaS platform once we have gone through the current application and the integrations you want to deliver first.

Most recently, I worked on React and Next.js delivery at WebIntegrator, while my previous work at EmbedIT involved banking interfaces, backend-for-frontend integrations and API contracts, which taught me to pay attention to how the frontend behaves when an integration is slow, returns incomplete data or fails. At Ersilia, I also worked on a scientific platform and AI-assisted document workflows, and I maintain my own React and TypeScript application with Supabase and real-time features.

I would like to understand which KlickTipp flows are already in place and which events the platform needs to exchange with it, so I can review the API and suggest a first milestone with clear acceptance criteria; I would also like to agree on the weekly schedule before making a commitment to a longer engagement.

I would be happy to walk you through relevant work or join a live coding interview, where I can show you how I reason about the code and turn a requirement into a working feature.

Best regards,
Lukáš

data.title: Take Over and Fix Our Existing Web App (React + Node.js)
data.description: Worldwide remote takeover of a React/Node.js/PostgreSQL order application without documentation. Broken Excel exports and email notifications, manual deployment; client wants repairs and a maintainable handover. Advertised fixed budget $1,500.
data.notes: Návrh připraven, nebyl odeslán. Inzerát a rozpočet znovu ověřit před podáním nabídky.
data.match_notes: Silná shoda React/Node/PostgreSQL a práce s existujícím kódem, API, testy a nasazením. Neznámý technický dluh a přístupy: nejprve nacenit ohraničené prověření, nepřislíbit opravu všeho za 1 500 USD. Veřejně přes 50 odpovědí.
data.proposal_text:
Hi,

Taking over an application without documentation is something I would approach by first making sure it can be run and understood safely, so before promising to fix everything within the advertised budget, I would suggest a small initial milestone to review the repository, reproduce the export and email problems and agree on what needs to be repaired.

React, Node.js and PostgreSQL are part of my stack, with recent experience covering React and Next.js delivery at WebIntegrator, banking interfaces and backend-for-frontend integrations at EmbedIT, and scientific workflows at Ersilia; I also maintain devShark, my own React and TypeScript application backed by Supabase, which means I am used to being responsible for what happens after a feature has been deployed.

For your application, I would want to trace an order through the API and database, check the export path and email provider logs, and understand the current deployment process before changing it, then cover the repaired behaviour with regression checks and leave a practical setup and deployment guide so the next change does not depend on knowledge held by one developer.

I would be glad to review a suitable part of the code with you during a call or work through a live coding exercise, so you can see how I investigate a problem before we agree on the repair milestones.

Best regards,
Lukáš

data.title: React UI & QA Development
data.description: Open remote project: implement React UI from Figma using existing REST APIs, with component/unit tests, CI, cross-browser QA and sprint test/defect reports. $15–25 USD/hour. Project 40703233.
data.notes: Návrh připraven, nebyl odeslán. Inzerát a rozpočet znovu ověřit před podáním nabídky.
data.match_notes: React/TypeScript, API a přístupnost odpovídají WebIntegrator a EmbedIT, testovací stack Vitest/Playwright. Stránka výslovně označuje remote, přijímané země ani časový překryv neupřesňuje: potvrdit práci z ČR. Sazbu neposílat automaticky; 28 veřejných nabídek.
data.proposal_text:
Hi,

Your emphasis on testing caught my attention because I would want the React interface and its verification to be delivered together, with the critical user journeys agreed early enough that the tests cover the behaviour your customers actually depend on.

Most recently, I worked with React and Next.js at WebIntegrator, including accessibility and CMS integration, after working on banking interfaces and API contracts at EmbedIT, where a component looking correct was only one part of the job and the loading, validation and failure states needed the same attention. React, TypeScript, REST APIs, Vitest and Playwright are all part of my stack, and I also build and maintain my own application, devShark, with authentication and real-time data.

I would start by reviewing the Figma designs and API responses with you, choose one complete user flow as the first milestone and connect its component and end-to-end checks to CI, while keeping a concise defect log and test notes that make it clear what was checked on desktop and mobile. It would also help to agree on the browser versions and the overlap you need with your team, as I work remotely from Prague.

I would be happy to show you relevant code and take part in a live coding interview so you can see how I build a component, investigate an edge case and test the result.

Best regards,
Lukáš

data.title: Flyenzo Flight Booking Platform Enhancements
data.description: Open remote Next.js flight-booking enhancements: seat-map synchronization, purchasable extras and cancellation refunds. TypeScript, Drizzle/Postgres, Redis locks, Stripe, Clerk and Playwright. $15–25 USD/hour; project 40701959.
data.notes: Návrh připraven, nebyl odeslán. Inzerát a rozpočet znovu ověřit před podáním nabídky.
data.match_notes: Velmi dobrá shoda Next/TS/PostgreSQL/Stripe/Drizzle/Redis a rezervační zkušenost Take a Break, plus cestovní kontext Kiwi.com. Nenárokovat dosavadní zkušenost s konkrétními Lua seat-locky nebo Clerk. Remote je uvedeno, podporované země a časový překryv je třeba potvrdit; 102 nabídek a nízká sazba.
data.proposal_text:
Hi,

The booking context makes this project particularly interesting to me because I have worked on a reservation application at Take a Break using Next.js, TypeScript, Node.js, PostgreSQL and Stripe, while my earlier work in travel support at Kiwi.com gave me a useful perspective on what a confusing booking or cancellation flow means for the person on the other side of the screen.

My more recent development work includes React and Next.js delivery at WebIntegrator and banking interfaces with API integrations at EmbedIT, and I also work with Drizzle, Redis and Playwright, so there is a strong overlap with the stack you described, although I would want to review your existing seat-lock and authentication implementation before proposing changes to it.

For the first milestone, I would suggest choosing one booking flow and defining its expected behaviour under concurrent use and retries, then implementing and testing the relevant changes against the existing payment and database paths; for the refund work, I would first ask you to confirm the fare rules and the cases that should require manual review, so those decisions are reflected in the code and its tests.

I work remotely from Prague and would be happy to agree on the necessary overlap, walk you through my booking-related work or take a live coding interview where I can show you how I approach this kind of implementation.

Best regards,
Lukáš

data.title: Front-End & Backend Build for HRTech
data.description: Open remote HR platform frontend with existing authentication and REST/GraphQL backend. React, TypeScript, modern CSS, staged UI delivery, Git reviews and automated tests. Advertised fixed budget INR 12,500–37,500, paid on delivery; project 40700417.
data.notes: Návrh připraven, nebyl odeslán. Inzerát a rozpočet znovu ověřit před podáním nabídky.
data.match_notes: React/TS, autentizace, datová rozhraní a přístupnost sedí. Název zmiňuje backend, ale popis říká existující backend: vyjasnit skutečný rozsah. Ověřit práci z ČR, nízký rozpočet a placení po dodání, domluvit menší financovaný milník; 144 nabídek.
data.proposal_text:
Hi,

Your description sounds like a good match for my frontend work because React and TypeScript are the technologies I use most, and I would be interested in building the interface around your existing authentication and APIs once we have confirmed which parts of the backend are already ready to use.

Most recently, I worked on React and Next.js applications at WebIntegrator with a focus on accessible interfaces and maintainable delivery, while at EmbedIT I built banking interfaces and backend-for-frontend integrations, where clear API contracts and reliable handling of user data were central to the work. I also build and maintain devShark, a React and TypeScript application with Supabase authentication and real-time data, and my portfolio at lukaskouril.dev contains more detail about these projects and my other experience.

I would suggest starting with the login and dashboard flow as a separately agreed milestone, so we can confirm the design direction, API integration and testing approach before expanding into the remaining screens; given the budget shown, I would want to clarify the total number of views and agree on a realistic scope and payment milestones first.

I work remotely from Prague and would be happy to show you my code or take part in a live coding interview, where you can see how I turn a requirement into a component and handle the less obvious states around it.

Best regards,
Lukáš
